video_title: Did Crypto Bottom in June? Why Bad News Has Stopped Mattering
gist: Bitwise CIO Matt Hogan argues crypto bottomed in June 2026 and is in an early multi-year bull market built on Bitcoin, stablecoins and tokenization, citing resilience to the $6.3B Binance hack and a Democratic blue wave. He lays out Bitwise's $1.6M-by-2036 Bitcoin math, the 'rule of eight' for institutional adoption, an edges-first view of tokenized stocks, and bullish takes on Hyperliquid, Near, Avalanche and Zcash.

themes.theme: Cycle call: June bottom, bad news stops mattering

insights.claim: Bitwise CIO Matt Hogan believes crypto bottomed in June 2026 and is in the early stage of a multi-year bull market resting on Bitcoin, stablecoins and tokenization.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Frames the drawdown as a buying window; June lows become the key invalidation level.
insights.quote: I think we're in the early stage of a bull market cycle. I think we bottomed in June.

insights.claim: Crypto's resilience to the $6.3B Binance hack, a Democratic blue wave in Congress, hot inflation prints and rising Fed hike expectations signals an early bull market, defined as the point when bad news stops mattering.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Use price reaction to negative news as a regime indicator; muted selloffs on bad headlines are bullish tells.
insights.quote: one definition of an early bull market is when bad news stops mattering.

insights.claim: Hogan is tactically pessimistic for the next few weeks due to uncertainty over the incoming Democratic Congress's crypto stance, but expects a good end of 2026.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Near-term chop may offer entries ahead of a stronger year-end.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's drop of roughly 40% from its high followed a momentum top near $125K, similar to gold's momentum-driven top and reset; Hogan sees both resets as noise within a long-term uptrend.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Treat the drawdown as a momentum reset rather than a broken thesis; gold appears to be turning first.

themes.theme: AI bubble scenarios and crypto-AI tokens

insights.claim: Hogan argues Bitcoin wins in three of four AI outcomes: AI utopia (scarce assets soar), AI bust with recession met by government bailout/stimulus, and a muddle-through where institutional adoption drives price; only a sharp recession with no government response would push Bitcoin below the June lows.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Bitcoin is positioned as a hedge robust to AI outcomes; the key risk to monitor is a recession without policy response.
insights.quote: heads we win tails we win. If the coin lands on its side we win as well.

insights.claim: In an AI-bust scenario Hogan sketches Anthropic pricing its IPO below $1 trillion, over-levered neoclouds going bust and a US recession because AI is adding 2-4% to GDP.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Anthropic IPO pricing and neocloud credit are watch items for AI-bubble stress that could spill into risk assets.

insights.claim: Crypto-AI tokens (e.g. Arthur Hayes's flop, Pearl's proof of useful work) are in a Cambrian-explosion experimental phase mixing real projects with hype and scams; Hogan expects real traction for agentic commerce to be a couple of years out and advises caution.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Size crypto-AI bets as speculative; the mainstream growth story for now is tokenization and stablecoins.
insights.quote: we're sort of in the the Cambrian explosion phase where there's going to be interesting projects and really junky hype scam projects

insights.claim: Bitwise is publicly bullish on Near because its core intents business is valuable on its own, making its agentic-finance AI vision effectively a free option.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Near offers AI upside without paying for it, a preferred structure for crypto-AI exposure.
insights.quote: you can make an investment in year and then get this speculative uh uh sparkly thing

insights.claim: Hogan favors Venice in crypto-AI because it shows organic end-user demand and real product-market fit rather than hype, while Pearl is too new for Bitwise to bring to institutions.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Filter crypto-AI tokens on organic usage growth; Venice is the consensus favored name among crypto insiders.

themes.theme: Washington: blue wave, Clarity Act, DeFi risk

insights.claim: Hogan thinks a Democratic Congress focused on ethics investigations into World Liberty Financial and Trumpcoin would be received extraordinarily favorably by crypto, since most in the industry see those ventures as having hurt it.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Ethics-focused Democratic oversight may be a non-event or positive, contrary to fears of a blue-wave selloff.

insights.claim: A combative Democratic Congress with riders limiting SEC rulemaking would be marginally negative for crypto overall, with DeFi uniquely at risk from efforts to strengthen the BRCA.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: DeFi tokens carry the most regulatory beta to the new Congress; underweight relative to Bitcoin if hostility rises.
insights.quote: So I think DeFi is uniquely at risk.

insights.claim: Despite the Clarity Act failing, Hogan argues crypto already got what it needs for the next two years: the Genius Act, a pro-crypto SEC and CFTC, and the ability for tokens to generate revenue, leaving the net outlook neutral to slightly positive.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Legislative failure is less material than markets fear; regulatory tailwinds via agencies persist.
insights.quote: I think generally speaking, crypto got everything it needed to succeed in the last 2 years.

insights.claim: Hogan expects crypto to become too big to fail within two years via stablecoin, tokenization and mainstream Bitcoin adoption, limiting how much a future Democratic administration in 2028 could roll back.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: The industry is on a two-year clock; adoption metrics through 2028 determine regulatory durability.
insights.quote: my guess is that crypto gets too big to fail in the next two years

insights.claim: Whether onchain finance splits into a walled-off US version and a rest-of-world version hinges on how Congress restricts DeFi protocols; Hogan expects long-term convergence via permissioned pools, automated compliance and identity.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Automated compliance and identity infrastructure is the enabling layer for a unified global onchain market.

insights.claim: Institutions are largely unconcerned by crypto hacks because they hold assets via ETFs and institutional cold-storage custodians whose track record has been exceptional; hacks mostly hurt crypto-native users on exchanges or with old storage.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Hack headlines are unlikely to slow institutional ETF flows.
insights.quote: the institutions haven't generally been concerned um about the hacks.

insights.claim: Across the 10 largest hacks in Bitcoin's history, the 30-day return afterward was up five times and down five times, showing hacks have little predictive price impact.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Don't trade hacks as directional Bitcoin signals; 30-day outcomes are a coin flip.
insights.quote: in five cases, Bitcoin is up, in five cases, Bitcoin is down.

insights.claim: The crypto buyer base has shifted from family offices and independent RIAs to the largest wealth platforms: Wells Fargo put Bitcoin into a model portfolio, JP Morgan added crypto to its long-term capital market assumptions, and Morgan Stanley launched its own Bitcoin ETFs.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Distribution through mega wealth platforms is a structural, sticky source of Bitcoin demand.

insights.claim: Hogan says he routinely addresses platforms with about $3 trillion of combined wealth in a single week, and pensions, consultants and sovereign wealth funds are only starting to come online.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: The pension/SWF wave is still ahead, implying further institutional flow upside.

insights.claim: Bitwise's 'rule of eight': the average client allocates after eight meetings, so quarterly meetings since the ETF launch about 2.5 years ago are only now reaching acceptance, and central banks meeting yearly will take about eight years.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Institutional adoption is a function of elapsed time; expect flows to accelerate as more allocators hit the eighth-meeting threshold.
insights.quote: our average client allocates to us after eight meetings.

insights.claim: Validation from DTCC, NASDAQ, BlackRock and others, plus debasement concerns and stablecoin/tokenization utility, help but adoption is mainly driven by the relentless passage of time, as with ETFs, index funds and private credit before.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Patience trade: financial innovations follow slow S-curves before broad allocation.

insights.claim: Hogan views quantum and AI threats to cryptography as mostly a migration risk rather than a meltdown risk, except for Satoshi-era and early Bitcoin coins, which will force a very challenging community debate soon.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Monitor Bitcoin developer forums on legacy-coin handling; a contentious debate could cause market ripples.
insights.quote: mostly a migration risk, not a meltdown risk.

insights.claim: Dozens of public companies opting out of tokenized trading is driven by board committees seeing only downside (pricing glitches, lawsuits) and free-riding on pioneers; Hogan says it doesn't matter long term.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Opt-outs are not a signal against tokenization; adoption will grow regardless.
insights.quote: the reason is that committees exist to say no.

insights.claim: Tokenized stock adoption over the next year or two will come from the edges, international investors lacking US stock access and hedge funds needing weekend trading, not from replacing US brokerage accounts; eventually all stocks will trade 24/7 and settle on public blockchains.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Look for tokenized equity volume growth offshore and among 24/7 traders, not US retail brokerages.
insights.quote: Eventually all stocks will be tokenized. Stocks will trade 24/7 365 and settle on public blockchains.

insights.claim: Avalanche being picked as the clearing ledger for a 24/7 tokenized stock venue keeps AVAX in the cohort of assets likely to participate in the next bull market, while some other alt L1s lacking business wins risk being left out of the 2027 bull market.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Business wins separate alt L1 winners from laggards; favor L1s with institutional deals.
insights.quote: certainly there are some other alt L1s who don't have that same level of momentum and are at risk of being put in the not 2027 bull market category.

insights.claim: Hogan lists Solana, Hyperliquid, Uniswap, Aave, Venice and Zcash alongside Avalanche as tokens clearly participating in the current crypto metas and expected to do well in a broad bull market.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: A working watchlist of names Bitwise's CIO considers cycle winners.

insights.claim: ICE placing multiple onchain bets (with OKX on X Layer and Trade XYZ on Hyperliquid) reflects smart diversification under uncertainty, akin to running an index fund, and shows it sees tokenization and stablecoins as finance's future.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Incumbent exchanges hedging across venues validates onchain market structure.

insights.claim: Hogan likens Hyperliquid to Amazon: a super app that started with crypto perps and is stacking growth lines in real-world assets, commodities and prediction markets, now open for others to build on and moving toward the US market.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Hyperliquid's layered growth curves make it a candidate financial juggernaut; US expansion is the next catalyst.

insights.claim: Only about 1% of wealth managers understand Trade XYZ and Hyperliquid, but that cutting edge views the nexus as one of the most exciting things in finance and is positioning for it.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Institutional awareness of onchain perps venues is nascent, leaving room for flows as understanding spreads.

insights.claim: Bitwise forecasts Bitcoin reaching $1.6 million by 2036, implying roughly 30% CAGR versus JP Morgan's 10% in its long-term capital market assumptions, which ranks Bitcoin as the top-performing asset of the next decade.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Major-house endorsement plus a 30% CAGR target frames Bitcoin as a core decade-long allocation.
insights.quote: We have a price prediction at Bitwise that it'll go to $1.6 million by 2036.

insights.claim: The $1.6M math: the store-of-value market (gold plus Bitcoin, about $30T) grew 13% a year from $2.5T in 2004 and would reach about $90T in a decade; Bitcoin rising from 5% to 25% share gets to $1.6M.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Track Bitcoin's share of the store-of-value market as the key driver of the long-term target.

insights.claim: Hogan calls JP Morgan including Bitcoin in its long-term capital market assumptions extraordinary, given its CEO once said he'd fire anyone who bought Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Signals Bitcoin breaking into the highest rooms of mainstream finance.

insights.claim: Debasement is a generational trade measured in years; with long-term yields near their highest since 2007, $2 trillion deficits during growth and rising economic populism, Hogan expects the debasement trade back in full force in 2027.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Position for renewed debasement flows into gold and Bitcoin in 2027.
insights.quote: I think the debasement trade will be back in sort of full force in 2027.

insights.claim: Hogan recommends owning both Bitcoin and Zcash: Bitcoin as the steadier institutional-adoption asset attracting most flows, Zcash as a smaller, higher-volatility momentum bet with possibly more absolute upside but lower risk-adjusted returns.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Pair a core Bitcoin position with a smaller Zcash satellite for privacy-meta upside.

insights.claim: As Bitcoin is dragged into the regulatory light, it makes room for privacy assets; Hogan suggests privacy could be 10-15% of the store-of-value market and that OG holders may sell Bitcoin to institutions and rotate into Zcash.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Institutionalization of Bitcoin is a tailwind, not a headwind, for privacy coins; watch OG rotation flows.
insights.quote: So selling sort of uh Bitcoin to institutions and buying Zcash, I think that's an element of what we'll see

insights.claim: Hogan sees privacy and institutional adoption as the two metas of this cycle, roughly an 80/20 split in their ability to bring flows into the market.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Weight portfolios toward institutional-adoption assets with a privacy sleeve.

insights.claim: Hogan was bearish on digital asset treasury companies, but data suggests DATs trade mostly as levered momentum Bitcoin, so premiums to NAV could return in another momentum boom; his base case is one large DAT per ecosystem evolving into businesses, with peak DAT likely past.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: DATs below NAV may be a levered rebound trade if momentum returns, but don't expect past capital-vacuum dynamics.
insights.quote: the data seem to suggest that uh, DATs mostly trade as a levered version of of momentum Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Token buybacks and burns have positive price attribution and signal alignment between projects and holders, while historically inflation/issuance cuts have been negative for performance.
insights.speaker: Matt Hogan (Bitwise CIO)
insights.so_what: Favor tokens with buyback programs; treat issuance cuts as a potential weakness signal rather than a catalyst.
insights.quote: I think it's pretty clear that buybacks work exceptionally well.
